en: end of a century; turn of a century

examples.ko: 그 소설은 세기말의 불안한 분위기를 그려요.
examples.en: That novel depicts the anxious mood of the end of the century.

examples.ko: 세기말에는 새 시대에 대한 기대가 컸어요.
examples.en: At the turn of the century, expectations for a new era were high.

examples.ko: 사람들은 세기말이 오면 세상이 끝날까 걱정했어요.
examples.en: People worried the world might end when the century turned.

examples.ko: 세기말 감성의 음악이 요즘 다시 유행해요.
examples.en: Music with a turn-of-the-century vibe is trending again.
I watched a movie with an end-of-an-era atmosphere.
Turn-of-the-century fashion is popular again these days.

explain: 한 세기가 끝나 갈 때를 말하는데, 한국에서는 보통 2000년을 앞둔 1990년대 말을 떠올려요. '세기말 감성'은 그 시절의 불안하면서도 화려한 분위기를 가리켜요.

phrases.en: This song has an end-of-century mood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 시대의 불안하고 화려한 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the anxious yet flashy feel of that era.

phrases.en: I like the 90s end-of-century vibe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘 젊은 사람들이 그 시절 느낌을 좋아할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when people like the feel of that time.

phrases.en: Mobile phones increased greatly in the late 90s.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국에서는 '세기말'이 보통 이 시기를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: In Korea, 세기말 usually points to this time.

explain_en: It means the time when a century is ending, and in Korea people usually picture the late 1990s before the year 2000. '세기말 감성' refers to the anxious yet flashy mood of that era.

examples.en: I still haven't heard from that person.

examples.ko: 아직껏 한국 음식을 먹어 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never tried Korean food until now.
You still haven't finished your homework?
I still can't forget that.
The rain still hasn't stopped.
My younger sibling is still sleeping.

explain: '아직'을 강하게 말하는 느낌이고, 보통 '아직도 안 했다'처럼 기대한 일이 지금까지 안 된 상황에 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '여태껏'이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '아직'이나 '아직도'를 더 많이 쓰고, '아직껏'은 조금 강조하거나 글에서 써요.

phrases.en: That person still hasn't come.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 자연스럽고 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural and common word in daily talk.

phrases.en: I didn't know that news until now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직껏과 뜻이 비슷하고 같은 -껏 계열이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to 아직껏, from the same -껏 group.

phrases.en: I still haven't done my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '못', '안'과 같은 부정 표현과 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with negatives like '못' and '안'.

explain_en: It is a stronger version of '아직' and is often used when something expected still hasn't happened. A similar word is '여태껏'. In everyday talk people usually say just '아직' or '아직도', and '아직껏' sounds more emphatic or written.

examples.en: The past life I saw in a dream was so vivid.
Some people believe in past lives.
Those two must have been connected since a past life.
My friend must have been a cat in a past life.
I watched a drama with a past-life story.
It is a story about a child with memories of a past life.

explain: 믿는지와 상관없이 일상 대화에서 비유로 자주 써요. 이상하게 잘 맞는 사람에게 '전생에 무슨 사이였을까'라고 농담해요. '전생'의 반대인 '내생'은 거의 안 쓰고, '이번 생'과 '다음 생'을 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 이런 좋은 사람들을 만나다니 전생에 나라를 구했나 봐요.
phrases.en: I must have saved a country in a past life
phrases.nuance_ko: 운이 아주 좋을 때 감탄하며 말해요. 정말 전생을 말하는 게 아니라 복이 많다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exclamation when you are very lucky. It is not about a real past life, just meaning you have great fortune.
phrases.en_equiv: I must have done something great in a past life

explain_en: Previous life in religious or folk belief (전생에 새였다) Whether or not people believe in it, it is often used figuratively in daily talk. For someone you click with strangely well, you joke '전생에 무슨 사이였을까' (what were we in a past life?). The opposite '내생' is rarely used; people say '이번 생' and '다음 생'.

examples.en: This is not too bad.

examples.ko: 날씨가 과히 춥지 않아서 산책하기 좋아요.
examples.en: The weather isn't too cold, so it's good for a walk.

examples.ko: 가격이 과히 비싸지 않으니까 한번 사 보세요.
examples.en: The price isn't too high, so try buying one.

examples.ko: 과히 어렵지 않은 문제라서 금방 풀었어요.
examples.en: It wasn't a very hard problem, so I solved it quickly.

examples.ko: 그 일은 과히 걱정하지 않으셔도 돼요.
examples.en: You don't need to worry too much about that.
It's a food I don't particularly like.

explain: 거의 '과히 ~지 않다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 써서 '그다지, 별로'에 가까운 느낌이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '그리'나 '별로'를 더 자주 말하는 편이에요.

phrases.en: Korean grammar isn't all that difficult.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 표현과 함께 써서 그다지 어렵지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with a negative, it means not all that difficult.

phrases.en: Please don't worry too much, it will work out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나치게 걱정하지 말라고 위로할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to comfort someone by telling them not to worry excessively.

phrases.en: This homework isn't very difficult.
phrases.nuance_ko: '과히'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 과히 but more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It is almost always paired with a negative, as in '과히 ~지 않다', and feels close to 'not very' or 'not particularly'. For the same meaning, people tend to say '그리' or '별로' more often.

en: to be strange; to be weird; to be bizarre

examples.en: That person's outfit is a bit weird.
I heard a strange sound at night.
The dream was so bizarre that I still remember it.
I bought a weird-looking fruit.
Isn't the story of that movie strange?
People often tell me I am weird.

explain: '이상하다'보다 느낌이 세고 조금 기분 나쁘거나 낯설다는 뜻이 섞여 있어요. 사람의 모습이나 성격에 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어서, 좋은 뜻으로 말하려면 '독특하다'나 '특이하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: A weird sound is coming from the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '괴상하다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 모양이에요. 소리, 꿈, 이야기와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun; goes well with sound, dream, or story.

phrases.en: That doll has a bizarre-looking face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양이 이상하게 보일 때 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for odd-looking shapes; it can be rude if said about a person.

phrases.example: 이 음식은 이름은 괴상하지만 맛은 괴상하지 않아요.
phrases.en: This food has a weird name, but it doesn't taste weird.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이에요. 생각보다 이상하지 않다고 안심시킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say something is not as strange as expected.

explain_en: Stronger and negative, grotesque looks or things. It is stronger than 이상하다 and carries a hint of uneasy or off-putting. Using it for a person's looks or character can be rude, so for a positive tone say 독특하다 or 특이하다 instead.

gh: general; odd, off, or not right

p.n: 이상하다 is milder and more general; 괴상하다 sounds bizarre or weird.

examples.en: That person looks refined in the way they dress.
Even though she is old, Grandmother has a graceful air.

examples.ko: 귀티 나는 얼굴이라서 부잣집 아들 같아요.
examples.en: He has such a refined face that he looks like a rich family's son.

examples.ko: 비싼 옷을 입는다고 귀티를 낼 수 있는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Wearing expensive clothes doesn't make you look classy.

examples.ko: 말투와 행동에서 귀티를 풍기는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people give off an air of class in how they speak and act.

examples.ko: 귀티도 타고난다는 말이 있지만 저는 노력이라고 생각해요.
examples.en: People say elegance is something you're born with, but I think it's effort.

explain: '부티'는 돈이 많아 보이는 느낌이고 '귀티'는 품위 있고 고급스러운 느낌이에요. 반대로 가난해 보이는 느낌은 '빈티'라고 해요. 보통 '귀티가 나다/흐르다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 귀티 나는 얼굴 덕분에 어디서나 눈에 띄어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to a refined-looking face, they stand out anywhere.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 사람의 얼굴이나 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-는', used to describe a person's face or look.

phrases.en: Refinement flows from my grandmother's way of speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 품위가 자연스럽게 느껴진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means refinement is felt naturally.

phrases.example: 그는 늘 귀티 나게 입고 다녀요.
phrases.en: He always dresses in a refined way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷차림이 고급스러워 보인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means one's clothing looks classy.

explain_en: '부티' is looking wealthy, while 귀티 is looking dignified and classy. The opposite, looking poor, is '빈티'. It is usually said as '귀티가 나다/흐르다'.

en: high and low; difference in level or pitch

examples.ko: 이 길은 높낮이가 심해서 걷기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This road has big ups and downs, so it's hard to walk.
Try reading with ups and downs in your voice.

examples.ko: 책상 높낮이를 조절할 수 있어서 편해요.
examples.en: The desk height can be adjusted, so it's comfortable.

examples.ko: 한국어 문장은 높낮이에 따라 뜻이 달라지기도 해요.
examples.en: In Korean, the meaning of a sentence can change depending on the pitch.

examples.ko: 땅의 높낮이를 맞추는 공사를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: They are doing work to even out the ground height.

examples.ko: 음의 높낮이가 일정하지 않아서 노래가 어려워요.
examples.en: The pitch isn't steady, so the song is hard.

explain: '높이'는 위로 얼마나 높은지만 말하고, '높낮이'는 높은 곳과 낮은 곳의 차이를 말해요. 땅이나 물건의 높이, 목소리와 음의 높고 낮음에 모두 써요. 발음은 [놈나지]로 'ㅍ'이 'ㅁ'처럼 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Each step has a different height, so you have to be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 곳과 낮은 곳의 차이를 말할 때 쓰는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A basic phrase for the difference between high and low places.

phrases.example: 이 책상은 높낮이를 조절할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can adjust the height of this desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 올리고 내릴 수 있는 물건에 써요. 책상, 의자, 침대 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for things that can be raised or lowered, like desks, chairs, and beds.

phrases.example: 노래할 때 음의 높낮이를 잘 맞춰야 해요.
phrases.en: When you sing, you have to get the pitch right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 높고 낮은 것을 말할 때 써요. 노래와 말하기에 모두 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how high or low a sound is. It works for both singing and speaking.

explain_en: Physical height or pitch variation — neutral, sound and surfaces. '높이' only says how high something is, while '높낮이' is the difference between high and low spots. It is used for the height of ground or objects and for the pitch of a voice or note. The pronunciation is [놈나지], where ㅍ changes to a sound like ㅁ.

examples.ko: 그렇게 단정적인 표현을 쓰면 오해할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use such definitive wording, people may misunderstand.
It's still too early to draw a definitive conclusion.

examples.ko: 그는 단정적인 말투로 자기 생각만 말했어요.
examples.en: He spoke only his own thoughts in a categorical tone.
In the news, you have to be careful with categorical reporting.
He was criticized because of his categorical remarks.
It's hard for me to say it with certainty yet.

explain: 확인하지 않고 딱 잘라 말하는 느낌이라 조금 부정적일 때가 많아요. '단정적인', '단정적으로'처럼 활용하고, 반대 느낌은 '유보적'이에요.

phrases.en: People felt uncomfortable because of the categorical way of speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱 잘라 말하는 방식을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a way of speaking that sounds absolutely certain.

phrases.example: 아직 모르는데 단정적으로 말하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: We don't know yet, so you shouldn't speak so definitively.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확실하지 않은데 확실한 것처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone speaks as if sure, though it isn't certain.

phrases.example: 이 글은 단정적이지 않아서 읽기 편해요.
phrases.en: This text isn't too categorical, so it's easy to read.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심스럽게 말한다는 뜻을 부정문으로 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used to say something is stated carefully.

explain_en: It carries a feel of speaking flatly without checking, so it is often a bit negative. It is used as '단정적인' or '단정적으로', and the opposite feel is '유보적' (reserved, non-committal).

en: to be abrupt; to be random

examples.en: Sorry for calling out of the blue.
What he said is so random.
A random question came up during the meeting.
This is out of nowhere, but are you free this evening?
Suddenly singing was a bit random.

examples.ko: 그는 뜬금없게도 시험 전날 이사를 했어요.
examples.en: Strangely out of the blue, he moved the day before the exam.

explain: '갑자기'는 일이 갑작스럽게 일어났다는 말이고, '뜬금없다'는 앞뒤 흐름과 맞지 않아서 이상하다는 느낌이 들어요. '뜬금없이', '뜬금없는'으로 가장 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I'm sorry I asked the teacher such an out-of-the-blue question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞의 이야기와 상관없는 질문일 때 써요. '뜬금없다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a question unrelated to the previous talk. It is the modifier form before a noun.

phrases.en: My friend's confession was so sudden that I was surprised.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아서/어서'로 이어서 놀라거나 당황한 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -아서/어서 it gives the reason for being surprised or confused.
phrases.en_equiv: I was surprised because it was abrupt

phrases.example: 그 이야기는 뜬금없지 않아요, 지난주에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: That story is not out of nowhere; it came up last week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'로 부정할 때 쓰는 활용이에요. 흐름에 맞는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form with -지 않다, meaning it fits the flow.

explain_en: Remarks or questions unrelated to the topic (뜬금없는 질문) '갑자기' just says something happened suddenly, but '뜬금없다' adds the feeling that it does not fit the situation at all. You mostly hear '뜬금없이' and '뜬금없는'.

t90.ax: What he said is so random.

en: to be unknown; to be elusive; to be obscure

examples.en: The whereabouts of the missing child are still unknown.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 연락이 끊긴 뒤로 소식이 묘연해요.
examples.en: Since contact was cut off, there's been no word about that person.
I'm worried because there's no trace of where my lost dog went.
For a while, nobody knew where my friend was.
Since there's no news, the family is very anxious.

examples.ko: 졸업 후에 선배 소식이 계속 묘연한가요?
examples.en: Is there still no news of our senior since graduation?

explain: 거의 '행방', '소식', '종적' 같은 말과 함께 쓰고, 어디 있는지 알 수 없을 때 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '연락이 안 돼요', '어디 갔는지 몰라요'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 사고 이후 그 배의 행방이 묘연해요.
phrases.en: The ship's whereabouts have been unknown since the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건이 어디 있는지 알 수 없을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for when someone or something's location is unknown.

phrases.en: The culprit's trail is still cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사라진 뒤 흔적도 찾기 힘들 때 써요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there is no trace after someone vanished; common in the news.

phrases.en: After we lost contact, news of him became unknown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 알던 것이 점점 알 수 없게 되었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something once known becomes unknown over time.

explain_en: It is used almost only with words like '행방' (whereabouts), '소식' (news) and '종적' (trace), when you cannot tell where someone or something is. It appears in news and writing; in daily talk people say '연락이 안 돼요' or '어디 갔는지 몰라요'.

en: to be glossy; to be greasy

examples.en: I ate greasy food and my lips are shiny.
My face was getting oily and shiny, so I fixed my makeup.
The newly painted floor gleams with a glossy shine.
My forehead is shiny because of sweat.
I went to the interview wearing shiny shoes.
He must have put on too much gel, because his hair looked greasy.

explain: 기름기나 물기 때문에 표면이 매끈하고 윤이 날 때 써요. 구두나 바닥에는 중립적이지만, 사람 얼굴이나 머리에는 기름져 보인다는 느낌이 있어요. 빛이 반짝이는 '반짝이다'와는 달라요.

phrases.example: 가게 안에 번들거리는 구두가 줄지어 놓여 있어요.
phrases.en: Rows of glossy shoes are lined up in the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건에 쓸 때는 윤이 나는 모양을 중립적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For objects, it neutrally describes a shiny surface.

phrases.en: I put oil on, so my hair is shiny.
phrases.nuance_ko: '번들거리다'와 같은 계열의 형용사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form from the same word family as 번들거리다.

phrases.example: 이 로션은 바르고 나서 번들거리지 않아요.
phrases.en: This lotion doesn't leave a greasy shine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 얼굴이 기름져 보이지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative, says the skin does not look oily.

explain_en: It is used when a surface looks smooth and shiny because of oil or moisture. It is neutral for shoes or floors, but for a person's face or hair it suggests an oily look. It differs from '반짝이다', which is about sparkling light.

en: to bulge; to protrude; to swell

examples.en: His pocket was bulging, so I was curious what was in it.

examples.ko: 배가 불룩한 걸 보니 많이 먹었나 봐요.
examples.en: Your belly is sticking out, so you must have eaten a lot.

examples.ko: 가방이 너무 불룩하면 지퍼가 닫히지 않아요.
examples.en: If the bag bulges too much, the zipper will not close.
My friend's belly is gradually getting bigger.

examples.ko: 지갑이 불룩하게 두툼해져서 바지 뒤가 불편해요.
examples.en: My wallet is so thick and bulging that the back of my pants feels uncomfortable.
The blanket was bulging, and then a cat came out.

explain: '불룩한 주머니', '배가 불룩해요'처럼 상태를 말할 때 많이 써요. 변하는 모습은 '불룩해지다'로 말해요. '볼록하다'보다 크고 묵직한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: After I put in lots of snacks, my bag started to bulge.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불룩하다'가 상태라면 '불룩해지다'는 그렇게 변해 가는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '불룩하다' is a state, while '불룩해지다' describes the change into that state.

phrases.example: 불룩한 배를 두드리며 잘 먹었다고 말했어요.
phrases.en: He patted his round belly and said he had eaten well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 '-ㄴ' 형태로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the '-ㄴ' form to describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: I have many books, so my bag is bulging.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주어 뒤에 서술어로 쓰는 가장 기본적인 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic polite form, used as a predicate after the subject.

explain_en: It is mostly used for a state, as in '불룩한 주머니' or '배가 불룩해요'. For the change, say '불룩해지다'. It feels bigger and heavier than '볼록하다'.

t90.ax: My friend's belly is gradually getting bigger.

examples.en: The pure white wedding dress is dazzling.

examples.ko: 눈이 내려서 온 마을이 순백으로 덮였어요.
examples.en: Snow fell and the whole village was covered in pure white.

examples.ko: 아기는 순백의 이불 위에서 곤히 잤어요.
examples.en: The baby slept soundly on a pure white blanket.
Pure white petals scattered in the wind.
She appeared dressed all in pure white.
This is a person with a heart as pure as white.

explain: 티끌 하나 없는 깨끗한 흰색을 말하고, '순백의 ~' 형태로 많이 써요. 순결하고 깨끗하다는 비유로도 쓰이며, 일상에서는 '새하얗다'나 '하얀색'을 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Pure white flowers are in full bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 티 없이 깨끗한 흰색을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a spotless, clean white.

phrases.en: Pure white snow covered the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '순백의 + 명사' 형태로 깨끗한 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '순백의 + noun' form gives a clean, pure feel.

phrases.en: It snowed, so the road is all white.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '순백'보다 '새하얗다'를 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, '새하얗다' is used more than '순백'.

explain_en: It means a spotless, clean white, and is often used in the form '순백의 ~'. It can also stand for purity and cleanness, while in daily talk people more often say '새하얗다' or '하얀색'.

t90.ax: She appeared dressed all in pure white.

examples.en: The misty lake looked mysterious.
That actor has a mysterious air about him.
The aurora in the night sky is truly mysterious.
I was drawn into the mysterious and beautiful music.

examples.ko: 작은 씨앗이 자라는 모습이 신비스럽게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Watching a tiny seed grow feels wondrous.
The inside of the cave was mysterious, but a little scary.

explain: '신비롭다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. '이상하다', '수상하다'는 나쁜 느낌이 있지만 '신비스럽다'는 알 수 없어서 궁금하고 아름답다는 좋은 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The night sky is really mysterious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 느낌을 말할 때 써요. 알 수 없어서 아름답다는 좋은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for sharing a feeling. It has the good feel of being beautiful and unknown.

phrases.en: I like mysterious stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신비스럽다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 글에서 조금 더 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 신비스럽다, a bit more common in writing.

phrases.en: The forest I saw for the first time felt mysterious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 느낌을 말할 때 '느껴지다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 느껴지다 to describe an impression you get.

explain_en: It is used almost the same as '신비롭다'. Unlike '이상하다' or '수상하다', which feel negative, '신비스럽다' feels positive: unknowable, intriguing and beautiful.

p.n: The other word is more poetic, full of mystical charm.
